igcse-0580-sketch-lines.description: Use intercepts and gradient to sketch any line with a readable axis scale.

sections.title: Which coordinate is zero at the y-axis?
sections.label: Y axis
sections.intro: A line meets the vertical axis when x is zero. Substitute that value to find the crossing.

blocks.html: Mark the y-intercept on the vertical axis.

figure.alt: A rising straight line with both intercepts marked.
figure.caption: The two marked points show where the line meets each axis.

blocks.prompt: Find the y-coordinate of the y-intercept of \(y=-8x+17\).
blocks.hint: Use x = 0 to find the y-intercept.
blocks.solution:
At the y-axis the x-coordinate is zero.

Substitute \(x=0\) into the line equation.

The answer is \(17\).

blocks.html: A y-intercept is a point with x-coordinate zero.

blocks.prompt: Find the y-coordinate of the y-intercept of \(y=-5x+21\).
blocks.hint: Use x = 0 to find the y-intercept.
blocks.solution:
At the y-axis the x-coordinate is zero.

Substitute \(x=0\) into the line equation.

The answer is \(21\).

sections.title: Which coordinate is zero at the x-axis?
sections.label: X axis
sections.intro: Set the vertical coordinate to zero. Solve for the horizontal coordinate.

blocks.html: Use both intercepts when they are different. If they coincide at the origin, find a separate point.

blocks.prompt: Find the x-intercept of \(y=2x+18\). Give its x-coordinate exactly.
blocks.hint: Set y to zero before solving for x.
blocks.solution:
At the x-axis, y is zero.

Set \(2x+18=0\) and divide by the coefficient of x.

The answer is \(-9\).

blocks.html: A line parallel to the horizontal axis may have no x-intercept.

blocks.prompt: Find the x-intercept of \(y=6x+22\). Give its x-coordinate exactly.
blocks.hint: Set y to zero before solving for x.
blocks.solution:
At the x-axis, y is zero.

Set \(6x+22=0\) and divide by the coefficient of x.

The answer is \(-\frac{11}{3}\).

sections.title: What does the gradient tell me about the line?
sections.label: Direction
sections.intro: A positive gradient rises to the right and a negative gradient falls to the right. A gradient of zero gives a horizontal line.

blocks.html: Rearrange to y = mx + c when possible to read gradient and intercept.

blocks.prompt: Find the gradient of \(9x+3y=57\).
blocks.hint: Make y the subject before reading its gradient.
blocks.solution:
Move the x term to the right. Then divide all terms by 3.

The line takes the form \(y=-3x+19\). The coefficient of x is the gradient.

The answer is \(-3\).

blocks.html: A vertical line has equation x = a. Its gradient is undefined.

blocks.prompt: Find the gradient of \(49x+7y=161\).
blocks.hint: Make y the subject before reading its gradient.
blocks.solution:
Move the x term to the right. Then divide all terms by 7.

The line takes the form \(y=-7x+23\). The coefficient of x is the gradient.

The answer is \(-7\).

examples.title: Find where a line crosses the y-axis
examples.question: Find the y-coordinate of the y-intercept of \(y=-5x+7\).
solution: At the y-axis the x-coordinate is zero.
Substitute \(x=0\) into the line equation.
The answer is \(7\).

examples.title: Find where a line crosses the y-axis
examples.question: Find the y-coordinate of the y-intercept of \(y=-2x+11\).
solution: At the y-axis the x-coordinate is zero.
Substitute \(x=0\) into the line equation.
The answer is \(11\).

examples.title: Find where a line crosses the x-axis
examples.question: Find the x-intercept of \(y=6x+8\). Give its x-coordinate exactly.
solution: At the x-axis, y is zero.
Set \(6x+8=0\) and divide by the coefficient of x.
The answer is \(-\frac{4}{3}\).

examples.title: Find where a line crosses the x-axis
examples.question: Find the x-intercept of \(y=3x+12\). Give its x-coordinate exactly.
solution: At the x-axis, y is zero.
Set \(3x+12=0\) and divide by the coefficient of x.
The answer is \(-4\).

examples.title: Read the gradient after rearranging
examples.question: Find the gradient of \(21x+3y=27\).
solution: Move the x term to the right. Then divide all terms by 3.
The line takes the form \(y=-7x+9\). The coefficient of x is the gradient.
The answer is \(-7\).

examples.title: Read the gradient after rearranging
examples.question: Find the gradient of \(28x+7y=91\).
solution: Move the x term to the right. Then divide all terms by 7.
The line takes the form \(y=-4x+13\). The coefficient of x is the gradient.
The answer is \(-4\).

extraPractice.solution:

glossary.definition: A crossing or meeting with an axis.
A point where the graph changes between increasing and decreasing.

igcse-0580-sketch-parabolas.description: Identify the opening direction, root positions and line of symmetry before drawing the parabola.

sections.title: Does the parabola open up or down?
sections.label: Open
sections.intro: Read the sign of the squared term. A positive leading coefficient makes both ends rise.

blocks.html: The sign controls whether the curve cups up or arches down.

figure.alt: An upward parabola through two roots and a dashed symmetry line.
figure.caption: The vertical mirror line is halfway between the two marked roots.

blocks.prompt: Does the graph of \(y=5(x+8)(x-6)\) open upwards or downwards?
blocks.hint: Read the multiplier on the product of the two x terms.
blocks.solution:
The coefficient of \(x^2\) is \(5\).

Its sign determines the direction of opening.

The factor roots are \(-8\) and \(6\). Mark their x-intercepts before drawing the shape.

Answer: Upwards.

blocks.html: The constant term identifies a vertical-axis crossing. It does not decide the opening direction.

blocks.prompt: Does the graph of \(y=4(x+5)(x-10)\) open upwards or downwards?
blocks.hint: Read the multiplier on the product of the two x terms.
blocks.solution:
The coefficient of \(x^2\) is \(4\).

Its sign determines the direction of opening.

The factor roots are \(-5\) and \(10\). Mark their x-intercepts before drawing the shape.

Answer: Upwards.

sections.title: Where is the vertical line of symmetry?
sections.label: Symmetry
sections.intro: The parabola has a vertical mirror line. If it has two roots, they lie at equal horizontal distances from this mirror line.

blocks.html: Find the mean of the two root values to locate the mirror line.

blocks.prompt: The graph \(y=-6(x+2)(x-7)\) is symmetric about a vertical line. Give the x-value of that line exactly.
blocks.hint: The axis of symmetry lies halfway between the two distinct roots.
blocks.solution:
The roots are \(-2\) and \(7\).

Find their midpoint: \(\frac{-2+7}{2}\).

The answer is \(\frac{5}{2}\).

blocks.html: A line of symmetry is a vertical line, not one of the roots.

blocks.prompt: The graph \(y=-5(x+6)(x-11)\) is symmetric about a vertical line. Give the x-value of that line exactly.
blocks.hint: The axis of symmetry lies halfway between the two distinct roots.
blocks.solution:
The roots are \(-6\) and \(11\).

Find their midpoint: \(\frac{-6+11}{2}\).

The answer is \(\frac{5}{2}\).

sections.title: Which crossing can I find without solving a quadratic?
sections.label: Intercept
sections.intro: At the y-axis, use x equal to zero. In the expanded form this leaves the constant. In the factorised form substitute into both brackets.

blocks.html: Write the y-intercept as a point and keep it separate from the x-intercepts.

blocks.prompt: Find the y-coordinate where \(y=2(x+3)(x-8)\) meets the y-axis.
blocks.hint: Set x to zero at the y-axis, even if the graph has two x-intercepts.
blocks.solution:
Use x = 0 in the factorised form. The two factor values are \(3\) and \(-8\).

Multiply the two values by \(2\).

The answer is \(-48\).

blocks.html: Use two roots to mark crossings only when they are real.

blocks.prompt: Find the y-coordinate where \(y=6(x+7)(x-12)\) meets the y-axis.
blocks.hint: Set x to zero at the y-axis, even if the graph has two x-intercepts.
blocks.solution:
Use x = 0 in the factorised form. The two factor values are \(7\) and \(-12\).

Multiply the two values by \(6\).

The answer is \(-504\).

examples.title: Choose the correct opening direction
examples.question: Sketch \(y=5(x+5)(x-7)\), showing the opening direction and both x-intercepts.
solution: The coefficient of \(x^2\) is \(5\).
Its sign determines the direction of opening.
The factor roots are \(-5\) and \(7\). Mark their x-intercepts before drawing the shape.

examples.title: Choose the correct opening direction
examples.question: Sketch \(y=4(x+2)(x-11)\), showing the opening direction and both x-intercepts.
solution: The coefficient of \(x^2\) is \(4\).

examples.title: Use symmetry between two roots
examples.question: The graph \(y=-6(x+6)(x-8)\) is symmetric about a vertical line. Give the x-value of that line exactly.
solution: The roots are \(-6\) and \(8\).
Find their midpoint: \(\frac{-6+8}{2}\).
The answer is \(1\).

examples.title: Use symmetry between two roots
examples.question: The graph \(y=-5(x+3)(x-12)\) is symmetric about a vertical line. Give the x-value of that line exactly.
solution: The roots are \(-3\) and \(12\).
Find their midpoint: \(\frac{-3+12}{2}\).
The answer is \(\frac{9}{2}\).

examples.title: Find where a parabola meets the y-axis
examples.question: Find the y-coordinate where \(y=2(x+7)(x-9)\) meets the y-axis.
solution: Use x = 0 in the factorised form. The two factor values are \(7\) and \(-9\).
Multiply the two values by \(2\).
The answer is \(-126\).

solution: Use x = 0 in the factorised form. The two factor values are \(4\) and \(-13\).
Multiply the two values by \(6\).
The answer is \(-312\).

igcse-0580-sketch-turning-points.description: Complete the square to locate a minimum or maximum and use it to guide the sketch.

sections.title: Which x gives the turning point?
sections.label: X
sections.intro: In completed-square form find the value of x where the whole bracket is zero. This is where the square makes no contribution.

blocks.html: Read the turning x-coordinate from the value that makes the bracket zero.

figure.alt: A downward parabola reaches its highest point at the marked vertex.
figure.caption: The turning point gives the maximum. The dashed line is the line of symmetry.

blocks.prompt: Use completing the square to find the x-coordinate of the turning point of \(y=-3x^2+36x-92\).
blocks.hint: The x-coordinate makes the bracket zero.
blocks.solution:
Take out the coefficient of \(x^2\) from the two x terms and complete the square.

The completed form is \(y=-3(x-6)^2+16\). The square is zero at the stated x-coordinate.

The answer is \(6\).

blocks.html: A negative sign inside the bracket can lead to a positive coordinate.

blocks.prompt: Use completing the square to find the x-coordinate of the turning point of \(y=-3x^2+60x-280\).
blocks.hint: The x-coordinate makes the bracket zero.
blocks.solution:
Take out the coefficient of \(x^2\) from the two x terms and complete the square.

The completed form is \(y=-3(x-10)^2+20\). The square is zero at the stated x-coordinate.

The answer is \(10\).

sections.title: Which y-value goes with that x?
sections.label: Y
sections.intro: When the squared bracket is zero, the other term gives the y-coordinate. Read the outside constant after completing the square.

blocks.html: Mark the turning point and use the vertical line through it for symmetry.

blocks.prompt: Use completing the square to find the minimum y-value of \(y=4x^2-56x+213\).
blocks.hint: Keep the outside coefficient when completing the square.
blocks.solution:
Completing the square gives \(y=4(x-7)^2+17\).

At the turning point the squared term is zero. The constant outside the square gives the y-value.

The answer is \(17\).

blocks.html: If a factor multiplies the bracket, keep track of it during every step of rearranging.

blocks.prompt: Use completing the square to find the minimum y-value of \(y=4x^2-16x+37\).
blocks.hint: Keep the outside coefficient when completing the square.
blocks.solution:
Completing the square gives \(y=4(x-2)^2+21\).

At the turning point the squared term is zero. The constant outside the square gives the y-value.

The answer is \(21\).

sections.title: Is this point a maximum or a minimum?
sections.label: Kind
sections.intro: The square is non-negative. A positive multiplier raises all other outputs; a negative one lowers them.

blocks.html: A positive leading term gives a minimum, a negative leading term gives a maximum.

blocks.prompt: Does \(y=-5(x-8)^2+18\) have a minimum or a maximum?
blocks.hint: With a negative multiplier, the square makes all other y-values smaller.
blocks.solution:
The squared bracket is never negative. The multiplier is \(-5\).

The graph's turning value occurs when the square is zero, so the point is \((8,18)\).

Answer: A maximum.

blocks.html: A parabola can have its turning point above, below or on the x-axis.

blocks.prompt: Does \(y=-5(x-3)^2+22\) have a minimum or a maximum?
blocks.hint: With a negative multiplier, the square makes all other y-values smaller.
blocks.solution:
The squared bracket is never negative. The multiplier is \(-5\).

The graph's turning value occurs when the square is zero, so the point is \((3,22)\).

Answer: A maximum.

igcse-0580-sketch-cubics.description: Look at the cube term, intercepts and the possible changes in direction between roots.

sections.title: How does a translated cubic meet the axes?
sections.label: Shift
sections.intro: Start from the basic increasing or decreasing cube curve. A constant added to it shifts every point vertically.

blocks.html: Use x equal to zero for the y-intercept. Use y equal to zero and a cube root to find the x-intercept.

figure.alt: A cubic crosses the horizontal axis three times.
figure.caption: Three distinct roots give three crossings.

blocks.prompt: What is the y-intercept value for \(y=-5x^3+15\)?
blocks.hint: Find where x is zero. A vertical shift changes the y-intercept.
blocks.solution:
At the y-axis the x-value is zero.

The cube term vanishes, leaving \(15\).

The answer is \(15\).

blocks.html: The graph of a positive cube has opposite end directions on the left and right.

blocks.prompt: What is the y-intercept value for \(y=-4x^3+19\)?
blocks.hint: Find where x is zero. A vertical shift changes the y-intercept.
blocks.solution:
At the y-axis the x-value is zero.

The cube term vanishes, leaving \(19\).

The answer is \(19\).

sections.title: How do three factors give three crossings?
sections.label: Roots
sections.intro: A product of three linear factors is zero when one factor is zero. Locate those x-values before sketching.

blocks.html: For three distinct roots, the graph crosses three times and changes direction between successive crossings.

blocks.prompt: Give the complete set of x-intercepts of \(y=6x(x+7)(x-6)\), as a set of x-values.
blocks.hint: Check all three factors, including x on its own.
blocks.solution:
At each x-intercept, the product of the three factors is zero.

Set each factor to zero. The three x-values are \(-7, 0, 6\).

blocks.html: If a factor occurs twice, the curve may touch the axis there. Mark repeated roots separately.

blocks.prompt: Give the complete set of x-intercepts of \(y=5x(x+2)(x-10)\), as a set of x-values.
blocks.hint: Check all three factors, including x on its own.
blocks.solution:
At each x-intercept, the product of the three factors is zero.

Set each factor to zero. The three x-values are \(-2, 0, 10\).

sections.title: What decides the far ends of the graph?
sections.label: Ends
sections.intro: Far from the origin, the cube term dominates the lower powers. The sign of its coefficient controls the direction.

blocks.html: A positive leading term rises to the right; a negative leading term falls to the right.

blocks.prompt: As x increases far to the right, does \(y=-2x(x+8)(x-7)\) rise or fall?
blocks.hint: Think about the highest power at a large positive input.
blocks.solution:
The highest power is a cube with coefficient \(-2\).

For large positive x, every x factor is positive, so the sign of the multiplier controls the right end.

Answer: It falls.

revision.body:
How does a translated cubic meet the axes?

Use x equal to zero for the y-intercept. Use y equal to zero and a cube root to find the x-intercept.

How do three factors give three crossings?

For three distinct roots, the graph crosses three times and changes direction between successive crossings.

What decides the far ends of the graph?

A positive leading term rises to the right; a negative leading term falls to the right.

igcse-0580-sketch-reciprocals.description: Locate an excluded x-value, two asymptotes and the correct side for each branch.

sections.title: What lines does a reciprocal approach?
sections.label: Asymptote
sections.intro: The graph is undefined at x equal to zero. On both sides, fractions with very large denominators get close to zero in size.

blocks.html: The line x = 0 is vertical. The added constant gives the horizontal line approached.

figure.alt: Two reciprocal branches with dashed horizontal and vertical asymptotes.
figure.caption: The curve approaches both dashed lines. The branches remain separate.

blocks.prompt: Give the y-value of the horizontal asymptote of \(y=\frac{-15}{x}+16\).
blocks.hint: A vertical shift moves the horizontal asymptote by the same amount.
blocks.solution:
For large positive or negative x, the fraction tends to zero.

The constant \(16\) is the value approached.

The answer is \(16\).

blocks.html: Draw two separate branches. Do not connect the graph at its excluded input.

blocks.prompt: Give the y-value of the horizontal asymptote of \(y=\frac{-2}{x}+20\).
blocks.hint: A vertical shift moves the horizontal asymptote by the same amount.

The constant \(20\) is the value approached.

The answer is \(20\).

sections.title: Can the curve cross the horizontal axis?
sections.label: Root
sections.intro: To locate an x-intercept set y to zero. Keep the condition that the denominator is non-zero while solving.

blocks.html: A crossing of the x-axis is different from crossing the horizontal asymptote.

blocks.prompt: Give the x-intercept of \(y=\frac{16}{x}+17\) as an exact x-coordinate.
blocks.hint: The line x = 0 is the vertical asymptote. It cannot give an intercept.
blocks.solution:
At an x-intercept use y = 0 and keep the condition that x is non-zero.

Multiply by x to obtain \(16+17x=0\). Solve and check the denominator.

The answer is \(-\frac{16}{17}\).

blocks.html: A line can be approached without being reached.

blocks.prompt: Give the x-intercept of \(y=\frac{3}{x}+21\) as an exact x-coordinate.
blocks.hint: The line x = 0 is the vertical asymptote. It cannot give an intercept.
blocks.solution:
At an x-intercept use y = 0 and keep the condition that x is non-zero.

Multiply by x to obtain \(3+21x=0\). Solve and check the denominator.

The answer is \(-\frac{1}{7}\).

sections.title: Which side of the asymptote is each branch on?
sections.label: Branches
sections.intro: Compare y with the height of the horizontal asymptote. The sign of the fraction gives the side.

blocks.html: For a positive numerator, the right branch stays above the horizontal asymptote. A negative numerator swaps the branches.

blocks.prompt: For positive x, is \(y=\frac{-17}{x}+18\) above or below its horizontal asymptote?
blocks.hint: Compare the graph's y-value with its asymptote, not with zero.
blocks.solution:
The difference from \(y=18\) is \(\frac{-17}{x}\).

The denominator is positive on the right. The sign of the numerator tells you which side of the asymptote the branch lies on.

Answer: Below.

blocks.html: The branches can be both above or below the x-axis over part of a sketch after shifting.

igcse-0580-sketch-exponentials.description: Use the base, vertical shift and value at x equal to zero to guide an exponential sketch.

sections.title: What happens at x equal to zero?
sections.label: Intercept
sections.intro: A positive base raised to zero is one. Multiply it by the outside coefficient, then add the shift.

blocks.html: The y-intercept is the outside coefficient plus the constant shift.

figure.alt: An increasing exponential rises past the vertical axis with a dashed asymptote below.
figure.caption: The left end approaches the dashed horizontal line. The green point marks the y-intercept.

blocks.prompt: Find the y-intercept value of \(y=3\left(\frac{1}{3}\right)^x-17\).
blocks.hint: A non-zero base to power zero is 1.
blocks.solution:
An exponential at x = 0 has a power equal to 1.

The y-intercept value is \(3-17\).

The answer is \(-14\).

blocks.html: The base to power zero is one, so the exponential term remains.

blocks.prompt: Find the y-intercept value of \(y=7\left(\frac{1}{3}\right)^x-21\).
blocks.hint: A non-zero base to power zero is 1.
blocks.solution:
An exponential at x = 0 has a power equal to 1.

The y-intercept value is \(7-21\).

The answer is \(-14\).

sections.title: Which horizontal line is approached?
sections.label: Approach
sections.intro: At one end the exponential term tends to zero. The rest of the expression is the constant shift.

blocks.html: Draw the shifted horizontal asymptote with a dashed line.

blocks.prompt: Give the y-value of the horizontal asymptote of \(y=4\left(4\right)^x-18\).
blocks.hint: Read the outside constant. The graph approaches a horizontal line.
blocks.solution:
At one end, the exponential term tends to zero.

The graph approaches \(y=-18\), the vertical shift from the x-axis.

The answer is \(-18\).

blocks.html: An exponential has no vertical asymptote in these forms.

blocks.prompt: Give the y-value of the horizontal asymptote of \(y=2\left(4\right)^x-22\).
blocks.hint: Read the outside constant. The graph approaches a horizontal line.
blocks.solution:
At one end, the exponential term tends to zero.

The graph approaches \(y=-22\), the vertical shift from the x-axis.

The answer is \(-22\).

sections.title: How can I tell whether it grows to the right?
sections.label: Trend
sections.intro: For a positive multiplier, a base bigger than one increases and a base between zero and one decreases.

blocks.html: Use the base first. A negative outside multiplier reverses the direction, and a vertical shift moves the whole curve.

blocks.prompt: Does \(y=5\left(\frac{1}{5}\right)^x-19\) increase or decrease to the right?
blocks.hint: A vertical shift does not change which way the graph goes.
blocks.solution:
The base is \(\frac{1}{5}\) and the outside multiplier is positive.

A base above one gives growth. A base between zero and one gives decay.

Answer: Decrease.

blocks.html: A vertical shift alone does not change the direction of the curve.

Answer: Decrease.
